paras: The killing of Steve Williams was the fatal shooting of an elderly Black man by bailiff Alfred Moree in a field at Isabella, Georgia, about noon on October 14, 1903. The only known report, a dispatch in the Savannah Morning News, called the killing justifiable on the information then available and said no arrest had been made.

Williams, whom the dispatch called "an old negro," was cutting grass in a field when Moree came to see him "about some costs he had against him." The report does not say what the costs were for or whether Moree was serving legal papers.

According to the Isabella dispatch, Williams, "becoming enraged," made for the bailiff with his grass blade, and Moree shot him. The first shot did not stop Williams, and Moree fired a second time, killing him instantly. This account is the only one in the coverage, and it gives no statement from Williams's family or from any other witness.
As of the dispatch dated October 15, "No arrest has been made." No report of an inquest, grand jury action or trial appears in the coverage.

The Savannah Morning News ran the story on page 3 on October 16 under the headline "Shot by a Bailiff," with the subhead "Old Negro Killed While Threatening the Officer." The dispatch put the bailiff's version as its own judgment, stating that "from the best information obtained so far, the killing was justifiable," while leaving open that later information might differ. No other white paper and no Black paper is known to have reported the killing.

accounts.label: Isabella dispatch (Savannah Morning News)
accounts.gist: Moree went to the field about costs he held against Williams; Williams, 'becoming enraged,' came at him with a grass blade, and Moree shot him twice. The dispatch judged the killing justifiable on the information then available.

framing.detail: Headlined 'Old Negro Killed While Threatening the Officer' and stated that 'the killing was justifiable,' giving only the bailiff's side.

info: About 12 o'clock on October 14, 1903 ('yesterday' in an Oct. 15 dispatch)
A field where Williams was cutting grass, at Isabella, Ga.
Steve Williams, described as 'an old negro'
No crime alleged; Moree went to see Williams 'about some costs he had against him'; the account says Williams then went at Moree with his grass blade

sources.note: Only report found: Isabella, Ga., Oct. 15 dispatch; bailiff Alfred Moree shot and killed 'an old negro,' Steve Williams, in a field over costs; called justifiable; no arrest.
quotes: Alfred Moree, a bailiff, shot and killed an old negro by the name of Steve Williams yesterday about 12 o'clock.
